title: Reserved GPU journeys and edge-case matrix
summary: Working writeup for the dedicated capacity console: focused on user journeys for creating reserved GPU pools, burst requests, autoscale policy UX, and a prioritized matrix of edge cases to cover in wireframes and e2e tests.
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Capture realistic user journeys for teams that reserve GPU capacity (monthly/annual) and occasionally request bursts or temporary reservations.
- Surface failure modes and UX affordances needed to avoid outages and bill shock.
- Provide wireframe notes for pool creation, policy editing, reservation timeline editor, and on-call escalation flows.

Assumptions:
- Customers can mix Dedicated and Hosted slots via routing policies.
- Billing preview API provides estimated cost delta for a given reservation duration.
- Pools are backed by different hardware classes (v100, a10, h100-ish).

Personas:
- Platform engineer (main persona) — sets up pools and scaling policies.
- Product engineer — requests burst capacity for experiments.
- Finance owner — watches committed utilization and cost commitments.

Primary flows (high level) with wireframe notes:
1) New pool quick-create (onboarding-first-run)
   - Left-most: contextual banner "Reserved capacity quickstart" with CTA "Create pool".
   - Stepper modal: 1) Name + team + region, 2) Hardware class selector (cards showing perf/cost), 3) Autoscale policy (toggle simple/advanced), 4) Reservation window (start/end or open-ended), 5) Billing preview.
   - Wireframe note: billing preview is a compact card on the right showing monthly commit, estimated committed utilization, and delta if burst allowance used.

2) Pool detail page (tabbed)
   - Tabs: Overview | Activity timeline | Reservations | Autoscale | Billing & SLA | Debug logs
   - Overview panel: live utilization sparkline, current concurrency, avg latency, current autoscale state, active reservations (chips).
   - Reservations tab: timeline editor with drag handles. UX requirement: show conflicts, overlaps, and suggested fallbacks.

3) Burst request flow (ad-hoc)
   - Product engineer submits a burst request form: pool target, num GPUs, start/end time, preflight check.
   - Preflight: capacity check + fallback suggestions (alternate region, hosted fallback).
   - Confirmation modal: shows estimated incremental cost and impact to committed utilization.

UX patterns and microcopy notes:
- Use neutral phrasing for failures: "Requested capacity unavailable — suggested alternatives".
- Expose an "Explain cost impact" link that opens a short breakdown (tokens vs reserved GPU hours).
- On reservations, show policy badges: "fixed", "preemptible-compatible", "burst-enabled".

Edge-case matrix (rows = user action, cols = system state) — each cell should be covered by wireframe or toast/alert copy:
- Create pool while quota limit reached -> inline quota error + link to request increase (mailto and jira link).
- Edit autoscale policy during active reservation -> warn about policy mismatch, offer "apply immediately" vs "apply after reservation" radio.
- Reservation overlaps another high-priority reservation -> show conflict modal with resolution suggestions (split, preempt lower priority, fallback to hosted).
- Burst request denied due to hardware mismatch -> show migration suggestion (recommend compatible hardware + perf delta).
- Pool destroyed while active reservations exist -> prevent delete unless force flag; force shows guaranteed fallback and billing warning.
- Billing API timeout during preview -> fallback to conservative estimate and show "Estimate may be higher/lower" badge.

Backlog grooming notes (prioritized):
- [P0] Timeline editor: drag-to-resize reservations + conflict visuals — 3 sp. (INF-4123).
- [P0] Preflight capacity check API hookup + succinct error UI — 5 sp.
- [P1] Billing preview component + cost breakdown overlay — 5 sp.
- [P1] Autoscale simple/advanced toggle + preset templates (low/medium/high throughput) — 3 sp.
- [P2] Onboarding quick-create modal and first-run checklist — 3 sp.
- [P2] Toasts for fallback routing when dedicated capacity unavailable — 2 sp.

Acceptance criteria (minimum):
- UI renders timeline with accurate reservation windows and conflict detection in staging.
- Billing preview returns within 2s for typical requests; UI shows conservative fallback if >2s.
- Burst preflight provides at least one fallback suggestion (region or hosted) when initial request cannot be satisfied.
- Autoscale policy edits surface potential impact to active reservations before applying.

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Should reservation expiry auto-extend if utilization above threshold? (ops and billing implications)
- How aggressive should cost conservatism be when billing API times out?
- Do we allow cross-region burst automatically or require explicit opt-in?

Wireframe sketch notes (for designers/dev handoff):
- Use lightweight timeline component with zoom (1h -> 30d) and day-grid snap.
- Reservation blocks: left label with owner/team, right-side 3-dot menu for edit/cancel/extend.
- Conflict overlay: semi-opaque red with suggested action buttons inline.
- Accessibility: color-blind friendly palette, keyboard resize of timeline blocks.

Testing and QA checklist:
- E2E: create pool -> create overlapping reservation -> verify conflict resolution flow.
- Load test: simulate 500 concurrent preflight checks to confirm API backpressure handling.
- Usability: 3 moderated sessions with platform engineers; capture time-to-complete pool creation.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Pair with billing team to define conservative fallback logic (owner: Marcus Chen).
- Add a small analytics event schema: reservation.create, reservation.edit, reservation.conflict_resolve, pool.delete_confirm.
- Draft copy for toast/alerts in content repo (PR referenced in linked_artifacts).

Design deliverables to request from UX:
- High-fidelity timeline component (desktop + responsive mobile).
- Confirmation modal variations for force-delete and policy-apply timing.
- Compact billing summary card to slot into creation modal.

Owner/next steps:
- Priya: consolidate this doc with INF-4123 notes and schedule design crit by 2025-02-24.
- Ethan: prototype timeline editor skeleton (React) and push branch for early feedback.
- Lina: draft microcopy for errors and toasts, add to content PR.

Unresolved technical constraints (for infra):
- Need an endpoint that can simulate reservation placement without committing capacity (dry-run).
- Need better telemetry for utilization percent per pool to support autoscale templates.

End of doc.
